Based at the club's training complex, [[Sportpark De Toekomst]], in [[Amsterdam]], it has competed in the [[Eerste Divisie]], the second tier of Dutch professional football, since 2013.{{cite web |url=http://www.ad.nl/ad/nl/5609/Eerste-divisie/article/detail/3446107/2013/05/23/Reserveteams-Ajax-en-Twente-in-Jupiler-League.dhtml |title=Reserveteams Ajax en Twente in Jupiler League |publisher=AD.nl |date=23 May 2013 |access-date=6 July 2013 |archive-date=3 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303210534/http://www.ad.nl/ad/nl/5609/Eerste-divisie/article/detail/3446107/2013/05/23/Reserveteams-Ajax-en-Twente-in-Jupiler-League.dhtml |url-status=live }} Jong Ajax is the only reserve side to have won a Dutch professional league title, claiming the [[2017–18 Eerste Divisie]] with a squad that included [[Noussair Mazraoui]], [[Noa Lang]] and [[Danilho Doekhi]]. Under national regulations, the team cannot be promoted to the [[Eredivisie]] or enter the [[KNVB Cup]]. Its primary purpose is to develop players for Ajax's senior squad."}}
